subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.
